evidence_notes: Judged from the eight named PNGs only: four committed plates at 1295x1061 and four 1400x1146 re-renders, matched to their sources by mean absolute pixel difference after resize (image-1 to the fine plate at 5.72, image-3 to the CPU standard plate at 5.47, image-5 to the full-axis plate at 5.43).
Border scan of every plate: 0 non-white pixels on the top, bottom, left and right edges, so no content is clipped at the canvas boundary.

Red-marker census of each plate found exactly three marks at consistent pixel positions: the conductor-only cross at (453, 548), the solved-field cross at (927, 245) and the solved-field axis triangle at (1005, 545), so the caption's claim that every lane carries the same conductor marker holds.

Ink census of each plate: about 19.0 percent of pixels carry ink; the lavender plasma region is about 7.4 percent of the canvas at mean RGB (218, 203, 236), a pale fill that recedes behind the contours.

The evidence caption is substantive rather than a restatement of the panel titles: it names the contour-level sharing, the reason the conductor-only panel has no axis marker, and the three lane views. It is not a finding.
The reviewed run's receipt records vacuum o_points_inside_wall = 0 and x_points_inside_wall = 1 per lane, which matches the single conductor-only cross drawn on every plate.

findings.summary: The newly added conductor-only cross marks a shallow discrete-grid saddle whose crossing the rendered contours do not show. At the marker (R = 1.818 m, Z = 0, about 82 mm inside the outboard wall at the midplane) the drawn contour levels are smooth, near-parallel arcs with no visible separatrix crossing, so a reader cannot verify the marker from the picture. The point is a genuine saddle of the stored vacuum flux (the census at line 769 finds min-in-R, max-in-Z about it), and the caption does name it, but the same painter's own curated documentation records spurious outboard-midplane census hits on labelled MAST solves, so a one-clause caption qualifier or a check on the census would let the reader trust it. Does not hold the figure: the caption is accurate as far as it goes, and no other mark is affected.

The flux contours render as very pale thin strokes: the contour ink is #999999 (about 2.85:1 against white) at a hairline width, and most of its anti-aliased pixels fall between 1.2:1 and 1.6:1, so in the outer field where contours are widely spaced the curves are barely visible at 900 px page width, while the black vessel outline carries far more visual weight. The field remains readable and no contour is lost, so this is a legibility margin rather than a defect; a slightly heavier contour stroke would let the field carry the weight the figure exists to show.

The panel plate is drawn on a 9.2 x 6.4 in canvas (1295 x 1061 px at 200 dpi, aspect 1.22:1), not the 14 in wide slide canvas the figure style rules declare, and the panel titles are set at 9 pt. The tighter canvas is defensible for two side-by-side square poloidal panels, and nothing is clipped or cramped as a result, so the plate reads well; it nonetheless departs from the declared default canvas, which a reader placing it beside other figures will notice.
